S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

patient_info.stressor: After the death of a longtime police colleague and chess partner, William responded in the way he knew best: tightening routines, simplifying meals, and treating food choices as another area where discipline could restore order. What began as careful budgeting and lighter eating during long advisory-project days gradually became persistent restriction, with his weight falling well below what was healthy for his age and build. Even as coworkers noticed the change, William framed it as professionalism and fitness, while privately judging his self-control and worth by the leanness he saw in the mirror and becoming fearful of regaining weight. He came to psychiatric care after an occupational health evaluation raised concern about his low weight and referred him for assessment before clearing him for continued field-related duties.

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: What brings me in is occupational health says I'm not eating enough, but most days I keep it to black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt or a few bites of chicken at night, because a full meal feels like I'm letting my standards slip.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: My uniform hangs off me now and I've had to tighten my belt past the old notches, but when the nurse said my weight was dangerously low I still thought, 'I could stand to be a little sharper.'

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If the scale is up even half a pound, I get this jolt like I've lost control, and I'll spend the day cutting back harder because I can't stand the idea of putting weight back on.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: When I look in the mirror, I don't see what everyone else says they see; I focus on my stomach and waist and judge the whole day by whether I look lean enough to respect myself.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: Occupational health has held up my clearance for field-related duties, and I can tell the team is second-guessing whether I’m fit to be out there. I’ve also stopped meeting people for meals because I don’t want questions or pressure about what I’m eating.
